concerns.message: The design says the pedestal at an island's highest-id dock 'differs from the rubbing source's dock'. In the slice that isn't true. The slice preset has sourcesPerIsland = 2, every slice island has exactly 2 docks, and `sourceSites` places source slot j at docks[j % docks.length]. So both docks of every island hold a source, and each pedestal shares its dock with source-i-1. The pedestals are separate objects from the sources, as §9 asks, but they don't have their own locations.
concerns.consequence: A worker who writes the `pedestalSites` unit test as 'pedestal dock is not a source dock' gets a test that can never pass. They may then 'fix' the site rule and break the settled decision, or report blocked. The test should assert 4 distinct docks, one per island, each the island's highest-id dock. The HUD at that dock has to show the E (collect) and F (inspect fruit) prompts together, and the browser test must expect both.

concerns.message: 'Tests pin the fruit deal with a test-only setting' has no matching pure operation. `createFruitState(sites, seed, preset)` only shuffles from a seed. There's no assignment constructor like the ledger's `createLedgerFromAssignment`.
concerns.consequence: The worker may wrongly report `blocked` for a missing pure operation. Two routes need no pure change: build a literal `FruitState` (the types are exported, and `checkFruitState` validates it), or search derived seeds (`fruit:<n>`) the way the pinned ruins search `ruins:<n>`. Either way, the test setting must be refused outside test mode, like the other test settings.

concerns.message: The plan says both clients get the kits in 'the duel start message', but there is no such message. Clients build the initial duel state from the sea duel's lobby schema (`createDuelState(defaultDuelConfig, { seed: lobby.seed })` in `apps/web/src/duelClient.ts:152` and `:208`, and the same pattern in test-tools' HeadlessClient). The lobby is created, and added to both fighters' views, when the grapple lands (`openSeaDuel`), not when the fight starts. Every place that builds a duel state needs the kits: `DuelMachine`'s constructor, the web session, the HUD fallback, the headless fighter, and the reconnect snapshot.
concerns.consequence: If any one of these still defaults to the Duelist mirror, the per-frame hash mismatches on every frame of an Ember or Smoke duel (acceptance #4 fails), or the HUD shows the wrong move names. Also, if the kits go into the lobby at reservation, the opponent learns them even when the encounter is later cancelled before the fight. Say which point counts as 'duel start' in the hidden-information test.

concerns.message: The `reserved` flag passed to `stepFruits` has to reflect this tick's encounter results. Sea duels, and the kits they carry, are created inside `stepEncounters` via `openSeaDuel`. The `held` set is computed at the start of `advance()`, before encounters run.
concerns.consequence: If the room fills `reserved` from `held`, a player whose 3 s channel completes on the same tick they're grappled eats the fruit after their duel was already created with the Duelist kit. They then fight that duel with the wrong kit, which breaks 'the eaten kit is used in every sea duel'. Compute `reserved` from the encounter or ledger state after `stepEncounters`.

concerns.message: The tap-versus-hold input is unspecified. If F is a latched world button like E and J (`keyboard.ts` LATCHED), the tap that opens the panel also reaches the server as a held tick. That produces `eat-started`, then `eat-interrupted`/`released` on the next tick. Also, the plan's list of panel reasons leaves out `released`, `moved`, `gap` and `left`, all of which the pure step emits. `eat-refused` repeats on every held tick.
concerns.consequence: The panel shows 'interrupted: released' right after it opens, or an unhandled reason. Forwarding every per-tick refusal as its own message floods the client at 20 Hz and can trip rate or size caps. Send changes only, and map every `FruitInterruptReason` and `FruitRefusalReason` to text.

concerns.message: `stepFruits` throws a `RangeError` for an unknown pedestal id or a duplicate player, and any throw inside `worldTick` calls `fault()`, which aborts the match (§12).
concerns.consequence: A bug in the room's dock-to-pedestal mapping, such as passing a dock id or a pedestal for an island without one, ends every live match instead of just failing an eat. Map dock → pedestal id with an explicit lookup that returns null otherwise, and unit-test it.

concerns.message: Workload and time limits. The branch table requires deleting each branch in parallel batches, and several of those runs must go through the integration or browser suites. Integration tests run in real time: 3 s eats, grapple countdowns, and a roughly 500-frame lost duel for 'kit survives defeat'. The browser suite uses fixed webServer ports, and the machine is shared. On top of that come the 4 carried ruins items and a new e2e scenario, all within a 3-hour worker deadline.
concerns.consequence: The worker is likely to run out of time on the branch table or hit port collisions when batching browser-level deletions. That leaves `untested` rows or a late `blocked`. Give each scratch copy its own port or run browser mutations one at a time, record the current integration duration first, and finish the table before polishing the arena drawing.

simpler_alternative: Treat F exactly like E: a world-input button bit, held and repeated through the existing input gate. Don't add a separate inspect request/response message. The first F press while moored at a pedestal's dock both starts the channel and makes the server send that player the pedestal's inspection once per mooring. The panel opens on that reply and shows the progress ring from the same channel; holding for 3 s eats, and letting go interrupts. This keeps every settled rule: F opens the panel, holding F for 3 s eats, and only the player at the dock who pressed F sees the kit. It also drops a new zod message, its rate limiter, the extra hidden-information path and the client-side tap-versus-hold logic.
cheap_experiment: Run a scratch tsx one-liner that prints `sourceSites(seaMap)` next to `islandDocks(seaMap, i)` and the proposed highest-id dock for each island. It will show whether every slice dock already holds a source, so every pedestal would share a dock with source-i-1. If so, the operator should confirm that's acceptable (§9 says pedestals are 'distinct from rubbing sources') before the worker writes `pedestalSites` and its unit test. In the same script, build a literal `FruitState` with a pinned Ember/Smoke deal and run it through `checkFruitState` and one `stepFruits` tick. That confirms the test-only pinned deal works without a pure-module change.
